question: In 2026, West Bengal became the last major State/UT to implement Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, completing its nationwide rollout. This made West Bengal the:
explanation: West Bengal became the 36th State/UT under PM-JAY (via an NHA–WB MoU), covering ~1.24 crore families and completing 100% national rollout. Health being a State subject, states opt in voluntarily.
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the Astra Mk-1, in the news in July 2026, consider the following statements:
explanation: All three correct. Astra Mk-1 is India's first indigenous BVRAAM (DRDO-developed, BDL-produced, ~Mach 4.5, ~100+ km, on the Su-30MKI); Indonesia became its first foreign buyer in July 2026.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Aastha Van Sanrakshan Yojana (AVSY), approved by the 7th National CAMPA Governing Body in July 2026, is intended for the:

options.text: Afforestation of urban commons around smart cities
Conservation and restoration of sacred groves, funded through CAMPA
Compensation of communities displaced by tiger reserves
Development of agroforestry on degraded farmland

explanation: AVSY is a Rs 3,000-crore, five-year scheme to conserve ~15,000 sacred groves ("Aastha Vans"), funded through National CAMPA (statutory under the CAF Act, 2016).
subject: Current Affairs

question: Consider the following statements about the India–New Zealand relationship, as advanced during PM Modi's July 2026 visit:
explanation: All three correct: Strategic Partnership upgrade, first Indian PM visit to NZ in 40 years, a Roadmap to 2030 plus concluded FTA negotiations (trade-doubling target ~NZ$7 bn by 2030).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Supreme Court's July 2026 ruling recognising the "right to walk" on safe, demarcated footpaths as a Fundamental Right derived it primarily from:
explanation: In *Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan* (2026 INSC 647), the Court grounded the right to walk in Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(d) (freedom of movement), with a correlative duty on urban local bodies.
subject: Current Affairs

question: In July 2026, China imposed a temporary export ban on which commodity, citing conflict in West Asia and the risk of global shortages — a move with direct implications for ISRO's launch programme and India's semiconductor push?
explanation: China banned helium exports (effective 10 July 2026). India imports almost all its helium; ISRO uses it to pressurise cryogenic/liquid fuel tanks and fabs need it for cooling and inert atmospheres.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Index of Services Production (ISP), launched on a trial basis in July 2026, is best described as:

options.text: An annual services survey conducted by NITI Aayog
A monthly volume index of services output released by MoSPI, with base year 2024-25
A sub-component of the Wholesale Price Index compiled by DPIIT
A quarterly index released by the RBI in its Financial Stability Report

explanation: ISP is a monthly volume index of services output released by MoSPI/NSO, base year 2024-25 — the services counterpart to the IIP (health and education excluded for now).
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the India–UK CETA, which entered into force on 15 July 2026, consider the following statements:
explanation: 1 and 3 correct. The UK zeroed duties on ~99% of Indian tariff lines on day one, and the DCC exemption is five years. Statement 2 is wrong — India cut duties on 90% of tariff lines (64.1% immediately), not all goods.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Vikram-1, in the news in July 2026 for its maiden orbital attempt (Mission *Aagaman*), is:

options.text: India's first privately built rocket ever to fly
India's first privately developed orbital-class launch vehicle, by Skyroot Aerospace
An ISRO small-satellite launch vehicle (SSLV) variant
A reusable booster developed by Agnikul Cosmos

explanation: Vikram-1 is India's first privately developed orbital-class launch vehicle (Skyroot Aerospace, ~350 kg to LEO). The first private Indian rocket to fly was Vikram-S (sub-orbital, Nov 2022), so (a) is wrong.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Which State recently became the first in India to enact a law granting women farmers independent legal recognition, delinked from land ownership?
explanation: The Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026 issues a 'Women Farmer Certificate' delinking farmer status from land ownership — a first in India.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The "SHANTI" vision unveiled by India in July 2026 is associated with:

options.text: India's campaign for a non-permanent UN Security Council seat for 2028–29

explanation: SHANTI = *Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity* — the theme of India's UNSC 2028–29 non-permanent-seat campaign, launched at UN HQ (EAM Jaishankar). India contests the Asia-Pacific seat against Tajikistan.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU-2026), cleared by the Cabinet in July 2026, seeks primarily to:

options.text: Boost India's urea exports to neighbouring countries
Add about 10 million tonnes of fresh gas-based urea capacity to cut import dependence
Bring urea under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) regime
Shift urea plants from natural gas to coal gasification

explanation: NIPU-2026 (Dept. of Fertilizers) targets ~10 MT of new gas-based urea capacity via 8–9 plants to cut import dependence. India is a urea *importer* (~30 MT vs ~40 MT demand); urea is *outside* NBS with a statutorily fixed MRP.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Consider the following statements about sacred groves in India:
explanation: All correct — sacred groves are in-situ conservation, can be notified as Community Reserves under the WLPA (added by the 2002 amendment), and Orans/Kavu/Sarna are regional names (Rajasthan/Kerala/Jharkhand).
subject: Environment

question: With reference to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund (managed by CAMPA), it is financed chiefly by:

options.text: Net Present Value (NPV) and compensatory-afforestation levies collected when forest land is diverted for non-forest use
Fifteenth Finance Commission grants earmarked for forests

explanation: CAMPA funds come chiefly from Net Present Value (NPV) and compensatory-afforestation charges levied when forest land is diverted, under the CAF Act, 2016 (90% to States, 10% Centre).
subject: Environment

question: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol relates to the phase-down of which class of substances?
explanation: The Kigali Amendment (2016) brought HFCs — potent greenhouse gases (though not ozone-depleters) — under the Montreal Protocol for phase-down.
subject: Environment

question: Consider the following statements about the Gangetic River Dolphin:
explanation: All correct — the Gangetic dolphin is India's National Aquatic Animal (2009), is in Schedule I of the WPA 1972, and is functionally blind, navigating by echolocation.
subject: Environment

question: With reference to in-situ and ex-situ conservation, which of the following are examples of *ex-situ* conservation?
explanation: Ex-situ = conservation *outside* the natural habitat: botanical gardens and seed/gene banks. Biosphere reserves and wildlife sanctuaries are in-situ (within the habitat).
subject: Environment

question: Which of the following statements about wetlands and the Ramsar Convention is/are correct?
explanation: All correct — Ramsar is the wetlands treaty; the Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites whose ecological character is threatened; India regulates wetlands under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017.
subject: Environment

question: The "nine planetary boundaries" framework — several of which are now breached — was originally proposed by a group of Earth-system scientists. Which of the following is NOT one of the nine planetary boundaries?
explanation: "Urban heat-island intensity" is not a planetary boundary. The nine are: climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, freshwater change, biogeochemical (N & P) flows, ocean acidification, atmospheric aerosol loading, stratospheric ozone depletion, and novel entities.
subject: Environment

question: Consider the following pairs of animal species and their prime habitat/State associations:
explanation: Only two. Asiatic Lion–Gir and Rhino–Kaziranga are correct; the Snow Leopard inhabits the high Himalaya/trans-Himalaya, not the Sundarbans (which is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger). RP1 — (i) China's temporary helium export ban (10 July 2026) — India imports nearly all its helium, so it squeezes ISRO's launch programme, semiconductor fabs and MRI cryogenics, reinforcing the critical-resources/strategic-autonomy theme. (ii) US Senate bill authorising up to 500% "secondary tariffs" on Russian-oil buyers — India (a top buyer of discounted Russian crude) faces an energy-security vs strategic-autonomy squeeze, sharpened by the lapse of the US Treasury general licence. RP2 — (i) PRAGATI — "Promoting Regenerative Agriculture Through Innovative Growth Initiatives," launched by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare to build ~20,000 agri-entrepreneurs for ~20 lakh smallholders.
